newsitem.title: GERMANY: Colonia eyes steady profit in non-life units in 97.
newsitem.headline: Colonia eyes steady profit in non-life units in 97.

text.p: German insurer Colonia AG said on Wednesday that it expects 1997 profits at its non-life insurer units to match last year's results.
"The bottom line is that we will have comparable results to those posted last year," Klaus-Dieter Laessker, Colonia's management board chairman said.
Premium income is expected to fall off between one and two percent and the group expects a moderate rise in claims.
Last year Colonia posted a net profit of 78 million marks, while Nordstern Allgemeine posted a 104.9 million mark net profit.
The group's fire and industrial insurance business is eyeing a seven percent drop in premium income with vehicle insurance premium income also dropping by some seven percent, the company said.
